complexity.explanation: Jump search combines the efficiency of binary search with the simplicity of linear search. It jumps ahead by √n steps, then performs linear search in the found block. Best case occurs when target is at the first jump position. Space complexity is O(1) as it uses only a few variables.

description.brief: An efficient searching algorithm for sorted arrays that jumps ahead by fixed steps, then performs linear search in the identified block.
detailed: Algorithm Analysis:
Time Complexity:
• Best case:    O(1)   - target found at first jump position
• Average case: O(√n) - optimal block size of √n
• Worst case:   O(√n) - target in last block or not found
Space Complexity: O(1) - constant extra space
Key Characteristics:
• Requires sorted input array
• Optimal block size is √n (mathematically proven)
• Better than linear search for large arrays
• Better locality of reference than binary search
• Fewer jumps than binary search's cache misses
Performance Metrics:
• Comparisons: At most √n + √n = 2√n
• Memory: Constant O(1) auxiliary space
• Cache Performance: Better than binary search
Comparison with Other Search Algorithms:
• Linear Search: O(n) but simpler, no sorting required
• Binary Search: O(log n) but more cache misses
• Exponential Search: Better for unbounded arrays
• Interpolation Search: O(log log n) average but needs uniform distribution

Using bit operations for block size in powers of 2
Cache-aligned block sizes for better performance
Early exit optimization when step exceeds array bounds
Hybrid approach: Use binary search within blocks for large blocks
Parallel block search for multi-core systems
use_cases: Searching in large sorted arrays with good cache locality
Database index lookup in block-based storage
Network packet inspection with fixed block sizes
Text search in large sorted dictionaries
disadvantages: Not as fast as binary search for large arrays (theoretically)
May skip over the target if block size is too large
Not suitable for dynamic data with frequent insertions/deletions
